lede: Corrales keeps Christmas on Corrales Road and around the Old San Ysidro Church, with a village tree lighting, an evening parade, a nativity festival and farolito lights at Casa San Ysidro.
celebrates: Corrales MainStreet runs the community calendar that lists the season. It opens with the Christmas Tree Lighting at the Corrales Village Complex, 4324 Corrales Road, on the same day as Small Business Saturday. The Starlight Parade follows on Corrales Road, with floats lining up at Wagner's and the parade traveling to the Recreation Center. Afterward St. Nick's Nite at the Jones Center, behind the post office, adds music, treats and hot air balloons. The Old San Ysidro Church, 966 Old Church Road, hosts the Festival of Nativities on a December weekend, and Casa San Ysidro, 973 Old Church Road, hosts Noche de Luces.

facts: Corrales sits in the Middle Rio Grande valley just north of Albuquerque, and its main street is Corrales Road, where the Starlight Parade runs. The Old San Ysidro Church on Old Church Road is the venue for the Festival of Nativities and is also used by the Corrales Historical Society for its Winter Craft Show, according to the MainStreet calendar. Casa San Ysidro, a short distance away on the same road, is run with the Albuquerque Museum and hosts Noche de Luces. The Village Complex on Corrales Road also holds the Village Council Chambers.
trains: Corrales has no train station of its own and no Christmas train ride that we could verify on a host page. Families who want a train day can look to the Albuquerque area. The Wheels Museum in Albuquerque covers transportation and railroad history, and the New Mexico Steam Locomotive and Railroad Historical Society is also based in Albuquerque. Check each museum's own site for holiday hours before a visit. Our Albuquerque guide lists the Trolley of Lights and other rides.

kidfact: Farolitos are paper bag lanterns with a candle inside, and they glow along walls and walks all over New Mexico at Christmas.
faq: Where are the main Christmas events in Corrales?

Most events are on or just off Corrales Road. The tree lighting is at the Corrales Village Complex, 4324 Corrales Road. The Starlight Parade travels Corrales Road from Wagner's to the Recreation Center. The Festival of Nativities is at the Old San Ysidro Church, 966 Old Church Road, and Noche de Luces is at Casa San Ysidro, 973 Old Church Road.

Yes. It is a public street parade, so watching is free. Families who want to enter a float can get a waiver from the Corrales MainStreet page or sign up at the lineup at Wagner's at 4:30 pm. The parade itself starts at 5:30 pm on the Saturday listed on the event card.
Who runs the Corrales Christmas calendar?

Corrales MainStreet keeps the community calendar at visitcorrales.com that lists the tree lighting, the Starlight Parade and the Festival of Nativities. Each entry gives the date, hours and place, with map and add to calendar links. We link every event back to that host page.
Can I see Santa in Corrales?

The official calendar lists St. Nick's Nite after the Starlight Parade, with music, treats and balloons. It does not state a Santa visit, so check the Corrales MainStreet page for the evening before you go if meeting Santa matters to your family.
Is there a Christmas Eve service in Corrales?
We do not have a Christmas Eve services page for Corrales. Albuquerque has one, and it lists services across the Albuquerque area.
